internal.title: Kafka Consumer Lag Alert in Accounting Service Resolved
internal.body:
At 12:17 UTC on 2026-11-08, a high Kafka consumer lag alert was triggered for the accounting service, indicating a backlog of approximately 5200 records. The investigation identified that the kafkaQueueProblems flag was enabled just before the alert, consistent with known issues causing queue backlog. The ops team disabled the kafkaQueueProblems flag at 12:37 UTC, which led to a rapid recovery and normalization of consumer lag metrics.

The elevated p95 latency observed was likely a consequence of the backlog rather than a separate root cause. Error injection was ruled out due to low error rates.

The incident was resolved by disabling the kafkaQueueProblems flag, and monitoring confirmed recovery shortly after the action was taken.

Timeline:
- 12:17 UTC: Alert received
- 12:37 UTC: Diagnosis confirmed queue backlog due to kafkaQueueProblems
- 12:37 UTC: Flag disabled
- 12:37 UTC: Recovery verified

Please review the lessons learned section for preventive measures and conditions under which similar issues may arise.

external.title: Temporary Processing Delay in Accounting Service
external.body: Between 12:17 and 12:37 UTC on November 8, 2026, the accounting service experienced a temporary processing delay due to a backlog in message consumption. This caused a delay in processing some transactions. The issue was identified and resolved within 20 minutes, and normal service was restored promptly. We apologize for any inconvenience caused and are taking steps to prevent similar occurrences in the future.
